[FMLA 17] Doppler — Doppler Effect

Observed frequency when source and observer move. The ROM uses one signed formula, not the textbook ± form.

Calculator scroll name: Doppler. Determines the frequency f heard by an observer when both source and observer are moving. The calculator does not offer a ± picker; it evaluates one signed formula.

formula
f=f1​⋅v−v1​v−u​

If the source runs toward you, more waves hit your ear each second (higher f). If it runs away, fewer waves arrive (lower f).

v is the speed of sound, f₁ the source frequency, v₁ the source speed, and u the observer speed. Casio takes u and v₁ positive in the direction of sound travel (source → observer). Source approaching the observer → v₁ positive; source receding → v₁ negative.

keys
FMLA→1→7

Primary inputs: f₁, v, u, v₁.

steps

How to run

  1. Press FMLA, then 1, then 7 (or scroll to the name and EXE)
  2. Enter each prompted value
  3. Read the observed frequency f

Example

  1. FMLA → 1 → 7
  2. Horn 256 Hz, sound 330 m/s, pedestrian at rest (u = 0), car 25 m/s
  3. 256 EXE 330 EXE 0 EXE 25 EXE → 276.9836 Hz (source approaching, v₁ = +25)
  4. Repeat last prompt as −25 EXE → 237.9718 Hz (source receding)
note

Official constraints: v ≠ v₁, f₁ > 0, and (v − u)/(v − v₁) > 0. Do not type textbook ± into this routine; map approach/recede onto the signs of u and v₁ instead.
